title: Nineveh: Assyrian Capital & Biblical Horizon
subtitle: Imperial archaeology, Jonah’s setting, and the 612 BCE fall
summary: Explore securely identified Nineveh as an Assyrian imperial city while separating its archaeology from the historicity/dating of Jonah and from any invented point for the city’s 612 BCE capture.
disclaimer: Nineveh is securely identified archaeologically. This scene does not claim that excavated palaces verify Jonah’s narrated events, nor does it place the 612 BCE battle at a precise point within the city.

whyShown.evidence: Nineveh is securely identified and preserves extensive Neo-Assyrian remains.
whyShown.inference: The city can be mapped as Jonah’s named destination without converting archaeology into proof of Jonah’s narrative.
whyShown.alternatives: Questions of Jonah’s genre, date, and historical reconstruction remain separate.

hotspots.label: 612 BCE city fall
hotspots.summary: Babylonian chronicle evidence anchors the capture of Nineveh historically while the detailed battlefield geometry remains unreconstructed.

whyShown.evidence: The fall of Nineveh in 612 BCE is independently attested in Babylonian chronicle evidence.
whyShown.inference: The city is the secure geographic anchor for the event.
whyShown.alternatives: The scene does not derive a street-by-street destruction sequence from Nahum or the chronicle.
